quarterly_data.signal: Customer Synnovis: in May 2026 SOPHiA announced a collaboration with Synnovis, one of England's leading pathology providers and a major provider for England's South East Genomic Medicine Service, to bring liquid biopsy testing to lung and breast cancer patients across the U.K. as part of NHS England's 'blood test-first' program, launching the MSK-ACCESS test powered with SOPHiA DDM. The company says the blood-based test can help fast-track cancer patients to targeted therapy up to two weeks earlier; following the successful pilot program, Synnovis is already supporting approximately several hundred patients per month with ctDNA liquid biopsy testing.
quarterly_data.figure: targeted therapy up to two weeks earlier; approximately several hundred patients per month

quarterly_data.signal: Guardant Health litigation over the MSK-ACCESS liquid biopsy test: the January 23, 2026 UPC Paris Local Division order rejected Guardant's application for provisional measures under three asserted patents (EP 3591073, EP 3443066 and EP 3766986) and Guardant withdrew its request on a fourth (EP 3470533). The UPC Court of Appeal's July 2, 2026 order dismissed Guardant's appeal on the ground of lack of urgency, without resolving the remaining questions of infringement and validity; should Guardant commence main (merits) proceedings, they would be entirely new proceedings. In the U.K., Guardant discontinued its EP 3470533 claims in March 2026 and introduced EP 3842551, which the EPO Opposition Division had revoked (not yet final pending any appeal); the U.K. proceedings remain pending with trial preparation ongoing. Legal expenses for the cases were $1.8 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026, net of reimbursements.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 legal expenses $1.8 million (net of reimbursements)
